writeup: TIC 469606998 is a candidate eclipsing binary star system with an orbital period of 5.428238 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry data. The primary eclipse produces a 3.53 percent dimming, while a secondary eclipse was detected at 6.1 sigma significance. The detection shows high statistical confidence with a BLS signal-to-noise ratio of 859.1, and pixel-level analysis confirms the signal originates from the target location, with a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 38.3. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel target. However, the eclipse depths alternate significantly between odd and even cycles, suggesting the underlying period may be twice the initial measurement - a pattern consistent with the corrected period of 5.428238 days presented here.
